doc.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Big band baseball teams
summary: Bands had baseball teams; Lester Young pitched, and Ziggy Elman's cigar disrupted a game against Harry James.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Oh, well, Basie was insane about him. Bob Bach played on their baseball team in Central Park. You know how bands had baseball teams in the old days?

Well I wasn’t there, it was before I came into Bob’s life, but my favorite thing was he said Lester Young was the pitcher. I thought this vague guy being a pitcher, that must have been some game. When Shorty, my first husband, was with Tommy Dorsey they had baseball games. And Harry James was this corny guy that took everything so seriously, and they came to play the Dorsey band in Bernardsville at Tommy Dorsey’s palatial estate. And they were kind of kidding around, the Dorsey band. But Harry James’ band were grimly serious. They had uniforms, and oh boy, you know. And our team was kidding around. And Ziggy Elman got up at bat and he had this big cigar in the way, it discombobulated the pitcher. Well there aren’t any more big bands so there aren’t any more ball games, but I guess that was kind of big in those days.
